headline: .NET Software Engineer
summary: .NET Software Engineer with over 4 years of professional experience building backend systems on the .NET platform. Comfortable writing complex SQL Server queries and designing RESTful APIs with ASP.NET Core. Practical experience with microservice architectures and cloud-native development on Azure. Skilled in containerizing and orchestrating services with Docker and Kubernetes, and in building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines with Azure DevOps.

experience.projectDescription: Microservice-based solution serving as a framework for integrating with various third-party services via REST APIs. The platform provides a plugin-like experience for end users, allowing configuration and maintenance of external service connections. Emphasis was placed on scalability, modularity, and reusability across multiple client-specific implementations.
highlights: Cut integration time for new external systems by roughly 60% by introducing standardized plugin interfaces and reusable components for common steps.
Led the migration from per-service Kubernetes deployment manifests to a unified Helm chart-based templating approach, reducing duplication across a dozen microservices.

experience.projectDescription: B2B platform providing end-to-end workforce management solutions for temporary staffing agencies in the Netherlands and across Europe. Includes tools for onboarding, time and contract management, payroll processing, and more.
highlights: Migrated a core microservice from in-memory caching to a distributed Redis cache, cutting memory usage roughly in half.
Modernized dependency management across a large monolith, upgrading well over 100 NuGet packages spanning dozens of projects.

projects.name: Agentic Job-Search Pipeline — .NET MCP Servers
projects.description: A set of ASP.NET Core services exposing the same functionality over both REST and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so LLM agents can call them as tools. Built to production standards rather than as a demo: unit tests, containerization, CI/CD and observability throughout.
